answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent checks confirm fraud. If votes are weighted by locked stake and rewards accrue only after useful work is verified, splitting one budget across many aliases adds no influence; buying influence instead ties up capital and risks forfeiture. An opal marketplace might price the lock in copper credits, pushing a sybil campaign toward its nadir: costly, visible exposure for little gain.
